new: // the minter is trusted about how long its own token lives

name: ACC1a-10-the-public-key-is-imported-extractable-and-signing
old: return await subtle.importKey('raw', bytes, { name: 'Ed25519' }, false, ['verify']);
new: return await subtle.importKey('raw', bytes, { name: 'Ed25519' }, true, ['verify']);
why: Extractable changes nothing an attacker can use: the key is PUBLIC, and its usages still exclude sign - which is the law the pin actually holds and which a mutation of `['verify']` would break. Recorded rather than dropped because the line reads like it matters and the next reader should know which half does.

name: ACC1a-14-the-minter-signs-what-it-cannot-verify

new: if (false) throw new TypeError('mintToken refused a claim set it could not verify');

name: ACC1a-15-a-signature-of-the-wrong-length-reaches-webcrypto
old: if (!sig || sig.length !== SIG_BYTES) return { ok: false, why: 'sig-shape' };
why: WebCrypto's own verify answers false for a 63-byte Ed25519 signature, so the refusal lands either way and no pin can tell the two apart from outside. The check is kept because it says NO before a crypto call rather than after one, which is the same reason the length bound above it exists.

name: ACC1a-17-F8-the-note-goes-back-to-saying-nothing-is-built
old: // ACC1d BUILT BOTH (2026-09-22), so the paragraphs above describe
new: // NOTHING HERE ENFORCES EITHER YET, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF SAYING SO:
note: ACC1a wrote that sentence while the refusal was unbuilt and it was true; the relay imports this file now, so it is a lie - DEPLOY-PROSE's shape exactly, and the shape this project keeps paying for. The gate derives membership from RELAY_GRAPH, so it cannot go stale by nobody remembering.

name: ACC1a-18-F8-the-note-drops-the-per-room-bound
